title: hybrid-tail-coalescer-and-spill-compression-pipeline-for-kv-cache
author: Asha Raman
description:
Motivation:
High spill frequency and fragmented free space in the KV cache increase disk/network IO and amplify tail latency for token-generating requests. This change introduces a hybrid approach to reduce fragmentation-driven spills and the volume of spilled bytes.

What this PR does (single-string description):
- Adds a Hybrid Tail Coalescer: a background compaction agent that identifies small "micro-holes" (free fragments under a threshold) at the tail of allocation arenas and coalesces them into contiguous spans when doing so minimizes copy work. The algorithm prefers tail-biased coalescing to avoid disrupting warm pages in the middle of arenas.
- Introduces a Spill Compression Pipeline: when eviction is necessary, pages eligible for spill are routed through an inline compression pipeline (lz4 fast, fallback to zstd for higher ratio when CPU slack is available). Compressed spill records are tagged with a compression header for backwards compatibility with existing spill readers.
- Eviction gating integrated with continuous batching: eviction decision now considers pending batch size and KV "recently-accessed" hints to avoid preemptive evictions that force immediate cache re-reads for requests in-flight. This reduces churn during busy tails.
- Kernel and scheduler hints: cache allocator exposes a small set of kernel hints (COLD/COLD_COMPRESS/CANDIDATE) to steer the runtime's kernel selection and IO batching heuristics.
- Telemetry and safety toggles: added metrics (spill_bytes_compressed, spill_compression_ratio, microhole_coalesce_runs, microhole_coalesce_bytes, eviction_gate_hold_ms) and config flags to control coalescer aggressiveness and enable compression per-tenant.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- The coalescer operates opportunistically and is bounded by a per-arena compaction budget to avoid CPU interference with inference. We tuned default budget to <2% CPU on a typical dedicated worker in our canary fleet.
- Compression reduces network egress and S3 object sizes for hosted spills but introduces CPU cost; we apply it selectively based on measured compressibility and runtime headroom.
- Backwards compatibility: spill readers accept both compressed and uncompressed formats; migration is opt-in via config to avoid step-change for large deployments.

Benchmarks (micro-bench on internal perf harness):
- p50 generation latency: ~0.6% improvement (noise), p95 generation latency: -9% on heavy-eviction scenario (50% cache pressure).
- Spill bytes written: -23% (lz4 fast baseline), observed zstd paths yield up to -42% bytes in high-compressibility workloads.
- Eviction frequency: -18% (fewer eviction events per minute in synthetic mixed workload).
- End-to-end cost projection: estimated 7–12% unit-cost reduction in cache-heavy workloads when compression enabled.

Rollout plan:
- Feature behind two-stage toggle: coalescer.enabled and spill.compression.enabled (tenant-level flags).
- Canary: enable coalescer without compression on 5 dedicated workers for 48h, monitor eviction and latency metrics.
- Stage rollout for compression on tenants with low CPU utilization or high spill bandwidth; monitor CPU and request SLOs.
- Full rollout after 14-day canary and a controlled canary expansion.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for coalescer (fragment identification and merge correctness).
- [x] Integration test for compressed spill roundtrip and backward compatibility.
- [x] Telemetry and dashboards (cost/latency/regression alerts).
- [x] Canary rollout plan documented.

Notes for reviewers: please focus on the coalescer budget interaction with our scheduler and the correctness of the compressed spill headers. I included a small compatibility shim to keep old spill readers functional; if we want to avoid the shim we can gate a short migration window in the control plane.

review_comments:
Benji Liao (review): Can the coalescer's budget be adjusted at runtime? We should be able to throttle if CPU climbs during peak.
Author: yes, it's a dynamic config and we default to conservative values. Added a note in ops config and a runbook entry.

Marta Kovac (review): I'm worried about interaction with existing defragmenter. How do they coordinate?
Author: Coalescer prefers tail regions and has a lease-based coordination token with the global defrag agent; added comments and a small unit test to validate non-overlap.

Diego Alvarez (review): Compression header looks fine but please add a version field to avoid future ambiguity.
Author: Added version byte and tests for reader fallback.

CI system: Build failed on first run due to flake in allocator test; reproducer added and fixed.
Author: fixed allocator race by adding a test-only barrier.
ci_checks: perf-regression-check: pass (no regressions on baseline workloads)
release_notes: Introduces a Hybrid Tail Coalescer to reduce fragmentation-driven spills and a selective Spill Compression Pipeline to lower spill bytes. Feature gated by config flags; enabled in canary before wider rollout.
notes: Observed canary showed stable CPU and reduced egress. Ops to watch spill_compression_ratio and eviction_gate_hold_ms for the first 72h after enabling per-tenant compression.
